topic.readerProblem: Compute transparent mention, recommendation, availability, and citation rates from an AI-answer audit export without hiding the denominator.
topic.connection: The package turns AI-search observations into inspectable metrics used to measure whether a brand is mentioned, recommended, and cited.

assessment: The article delivers a runnable local metric package rather than a blank template. It keeps missing answers separate from measured zeroes, exposes both citation denominators, labels every sample row synthetic, and does not present fixture output as provider performance.

sources.supports: SQLite aggregate-function behavior used for the numerator and denominator queries.
SQLite common-table-expression syntax used to make metric stages inspectable.
Standard-library CSV parsing and writing behavior used by the runner.
Standard-library in-memory SQLite interface used by the runner.
Provenance model supporting retention of entities, activities, and agents behind metrics.
Context and limitation documentation for AI measurement and governance.

checks: Ran the Python 3.9 runner against the populated CSV and compared all 24 generated rows byte-for-byte with the expected output after fixing deterministic LF line endings.
Read the final article and verified that unavailable answers, zero citations, mentions, recommendations, and the two citation denominators are not conflated.
Opened every external source URL and confirmed HTTP 200, then checked all five internal article links and five downloadable resource links exist.

artifacts.description: A populated synthetic audit export containing missing answers and measured citation zeroes.
A runnable SQLite query pack with explicit numerators and denominators for answer and citation metrics.
A dependency-free Python 3.9 CSV importer and SQLite query runner.
The checked 24-row result used for byte-level regression comparison.

methodology: The package imports sixteen explicitly synthetic answer-level rows into an in-memory SQLite table, executes two named SQL sections, writes deterministic CSV, and compares the 24 output rows with a checked fixture. Editorial review recomputed the documented example rates from the source rows.
limitations: The fixture is not live provider data or a benchmark. The package cannot judge source support, causal ranking, sampling quality, or whether a future answer will repeat.
